question.text: 'Vindhya Credit' Cat II AIF has signed a side letter with one LP granting enhanced reporting rights. The chapter's guidance on side letters states:

answer.text: All side letters are prohibited under SEBI (AIF) Regulations
Side letters are permitted only for foreign institutional investors
Side letters must be approved by SEBI for every LP individually
The existence of a side letter should have objective justification, and MFN usage should be regularised so that investors are not afforded special/additional rights arbitrarily

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.7.1 and Ch 11.8, the existence of a side letter should have objective justification (size of commitment, regulatory carve-outs, etc.), and MFN usage should be regularised so investors are not arbitrarily favoured. Side letters are permitted but must fit this framework. The Trap: Side letters are NOT prohibited. SEBI does not approve each individually. Foreign-only restriction is invented. Cross-Exam Context: Side-letter governance tested across XIX-A, XIX-B, XIX-C. Manager's Pro-Tip: Classify side-letter rights into (i) economic (MFN-able, usually), (ii) informational (MFN-able case-by-case), (iii) regulatory (e.g., ERISA, SWF specific — not MFN-able). This taxonomy simplifies the MFN election response letter.
